subject.title: Gateway silently skips channel initialization on plugin/runtime mismatch or missing module files

question: What startup contract should Gateway enforce when a configured channel plugin fails before channel registration?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the right behavior is a policy choice: fail-fast can break existing setups, warn-and-continue preserves availability, and hot reload conflicts with the current process-stable plugin metadata contract.

options.title: Warn and audit configured channels
options.body: Add a non-fatal startup audit/status summary for configured channels that were expected but missing, blocked, or failed setup/runtime registration, while preserving restart-required plugin metadata.

options.title: Fail fast for configured channel failures
options.body: Treat incompatible or unloadable configured channel plugins as startup-blocking errors, accepting the upgrade risk that one bad channel can stop Gateway readiness.

options.title: Split broader feature requests
options.body: Keep this issue focused on startup diagnostics and move hot reload plus broad performance caching to separately sponsored roadmap work.

recommendation.title: Warn and audit configured channels
recommendation.body: Add a non-fatal startup audit/status summary for configured channels that were expected but missing, blocked, or failed setup/runtime registration, while preserving restart-required plugin metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent bundled channel and Gateway startup work plus adjacent Feishu runtime changes make this the best available routing owner for the startup-contract decision.
